title: Sell Mineral Rights in Noxen, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Noxen, PA
metaDescription: Noxen, Wyoming County mineral owner in the dry-gas Marcellus? We buy oil and gas rights near the Meshoppen Creek valley, straightforward cash offers.
heroLead: Noxen sits up along Bowman Creek in Wyoming County, deep in Pennsylvania's dry-gas Marcellus, where the play runs thick and the wells have historically been some of the most productive per lateral foot in the whole state.
intro: Wyoming County was one of the counties where the big dry-gas operators moved fast during the boom years, and Noxen families ended up with leases and units that in some cases produced far beyond what anyone expected in 2009 or 2010. If your family signed one of those early leases, there's a decent chance the well has already gone through its steepest decline, and the royalty check you're getting now looks a lot smaller than it did the first couple years.

sections.heading: Why Dry-Gas Decline Changes the Math
paragraphs: Marcellus dry-gas wells in this part of the state tend to produce hard early and then taper off steadily, which means a royalty stream that looked strong in year one can be a third of that by year five or six. When we make an offer on a Noxen interest, we're pricing against where that decline curve is now and where it's likely headed, not against the number on your first-year statement.

That's also why some owners choose to sell rather than hold — a lump sum today locks in value against a well that's only going to keep declining, instead of collecting smaller checks for years while hoping for a refrac or offset well that may never come.

sections.heading: Getting Past a Confusing Royalty Statement
paragraphs: We hear from Noxen owners who can't make sense of the deductions taken off their check every month — post-production costs for gathering and compression that weren't spelled out clearly when the original lease was signed. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act guarantees a 1/8 floor, but plenty of Wyoming County leases from the early boom allow deductions above that floor, and we'll go through your statement with you line by line if you want a second set of eyes before deciding anything.

faqs.question: Is my Noxen interest still worth anything if production has declined?
faqs.answer: Yes, declining wells still hold value, just priced lower against the production curve than they would have been in the early years. We can give you a number reflecting current activity.

faqs.question: How do I find my lease if I don't have a copy?
faqs.answer: We check the Wyoming County recorder of deeds records for the recorded lease and any assignments before we quote a number.

faqs.question: Does selling stop future royalty payments to my family?
faqs.answer: Yes, once a sale closes, future payments go to us as the new owner. That's the tradeoff for the upfront cash payment.
